sections.text: Widgets solved the open-the-app problem for weather, calendars, and reminders years ago. A **bible verse widget iphone** setup finally does the same for Scripture — instead of opening an app to check today's verse, it just sits there, on the lock screen or the home screen, always current. FaithWall is the app built specifically for that job: a themed verse rotates in on its own, no daily swap, no screenshot-and-crop routine.

Haven't picked a lock screen app yet? [Our ranked lock screen app list](/best-bible-verse-lock-screen-apps) compares the wallpaper apps broadly — this post is about the widget format specifically, and how to get it right.
Widget or wallpaper — what's actually different

A **wallpaper** is a static image you set once and look at until you change it. A **widget** is a small live block of content that can update on its own schedule — today's verse, a streak counter, a date — without you touching the lock screen at all. Wallpapers don't move until you move them; widgets do the moving for you.

items: **Wallpaper** — best for one anchor verse you want to sit with for a season, full-bleed and unmissable.
**Lock screen widget** — small, glanceable, lives above or below the clock; best for a daily-rotating verse.
**Home screen widget** — bigger, sits among your apps; best when you check your home screen more than your lock screen.

sections.text: The 60-second FaithWall widget setup
Setting up a rotating verse widget takes five taps.

items: Download **FaithWall** from the App Store — free, no account required.
Open the app and pick a starter pack: Peace, Strength, Gratitude, or browse by book.
Choose the lock screen widget for daily rotation above the clock, or the home screen widget for a bigger tile.

Rotation runs on its own from here — swap packs anytime by long-pressing again.

The Bible verse widgets worth using

Three widgets are worth the real estate: a themed verse widget, YouVersion's Verse of the Day widget, and Dwell's audio shortcut — and only one of them changes on its own without you opening an app first.

items: **FaithWall's verse widget** — for the lock screen or home screen, rotating automatically through a pack you pick once. The pick if you want a verse that actually changes without you touching it.

**YouVersion's Verse of the Day widget** — home screen only, and it refreshes on the app's own daily cycle rather than a pack you choose. Good if you're already reading in YouVersion and want the same verse to follow you out of the app.

**Dwell's audio widget** — a one-tap shortcut into a listening session, not a text widget at all. It's solving a different job entirely — hearing Scripture, not seeing it — worth pairing with a verse widget, not choosing instead of one.

If you're layering the widget on top of an actual reading plan, the [Bible reading plan widget guide](/blog/bible-reading-plan-widget-iphone) covers the input side — this post is about the standalone verse, not the day's chapter.
StandBy mode and the case for a scripture widget lock screen

StandBy turns a charging iPhone, set sideways, into a small always-on display — and a **scripture widget lock screen** setup is one of the better things to put on it. Prop the phone up overnight or on a desk stand, and a rotating verse sits there in landscape the whole time you're not holding the phone — a second surface most people never think to use for Scripture at all.

Where this gets hard

Two problems sink most DIY widget attempts. **Curation effort** — picking the right verse for today requires knowing the Bible well enough to choose one, which is exactly the barrier a widget is supposed to remove. **FaithWall solves this** with themed packs (Anxiety, Strength, Gratitude, Grief) so the choosing is already done. **Rotation breaks by week two** — a widget you manually refresh from a screenshot dies the same way a manual wallpaper does; a themed pack keeps rotating on its own, still fresh a month in, not just on day one.

sections.content: Built for the small-tile constraints from the start, not a screenshot squeezed into a widget frame — text doesn't crowd the clock or clip at the edge.

Frequently Asked Questions
How do I add a Bible verse widget to my iPhone?

For a **bible verse widget iphone** setup, download FaithWall, pick a themed pack, then long-press your lock screen or home screen, tap the +, and place the widget — it rotates through your pack automatically.
Does a Bible verse widget update automatically?

A widget built around a rotating pack does — it cycles on its own. Widgets built around a screenshot or a manually-saved image don't update at all until you replace them by hand, which is the habit that tends to die first.
Can I put a Bible verse widget on both the lock screen and home screen?
Yes. Add the widget in both places — a small one above the lock screen clock and a larger one on the home screen — and both rotate from the same pack, so the verse stays consistent wherever you look.
What's the difference between a Bible verse widget and a Bible verse wallpaper?

A wallpaper is the full background image, set once until you change it. A widget is a small live tile layered on top that can update on its own — most setups support both, and most people run a wallpaper for one anchor verse plus a widget for daily rotation.
